name: 8cc
reason: README states 'Generated code is usually 2x or more slower than GCC' and 'It's not an optimizing compiler'; project is archived (successor chibicc) and makes no claim of being faster than any named baseline. No benchmark numbers, no shootout where it wins.

name: Argh!
listed_description: A minimalist, frustration-free, header-only argument handler.
reason: README and repo page contain no benchmarks or speed claims versus getopt or Boost.Program_options; the pitch is simplicity and no dependencies, not speed.

name: c
listed_description: Compile and execute C "scripts" in one go!
reason: Shell wrapper with a result cache; README talks about speed of C in general and 'see it run instantly' but gives no timing numbers against tcc -run, plain gcc or any other baseline.

name: debug
reason: README has no benchmarks or speed claims versus gdb, lldb or plain printf; it is an ergonomics macro header.

name: Fil-C
listed_description: a fanatically compatible memory-safe implementation of C and C++.
reason: Memory-safe C/C++ that is slower than plain clang C (search snippets of the project site and LWN quote roughly 1x to 4x overhead; fil-c.org itself was EGRESS_BLOCKED). The repo README makes no faster-than claim against any baseline (ASan, HWAsan, MTE comparisons are qualitative about safety, not speed) and holds no comparative benchmark results.
